subject: Scope sync: SOC 2 / bridge letter and subprocessors for Aurora Health
messages:
From: Elena Soto <elena.soto@aurorahealth.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@aurorahealth.com
Date: Sat, 15 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: SOC 2 Type II + bridge letter + subprocessor list (Aurora onboarding)

Hi Sofia,

We're onboarding Redwood for a patient-data adjacent workload and our security team needs the following to complete the vendor risk review by Aug 25: 
- Most recent SOC 2 Type II report (last 12 months) or a bridge letter if the report period doesn't cover Jan-Jun 2026.
- A short bridge-letter style confirmation stating Redwood's production environment was covered or that controls were materially unchanged since the last report.
- Full subprocessor list for any cloud or managed services used in production (including which subprocessors are covered by Redwood's vendor SOCs).
- Clarification on whether Redwood's SOC is carve-out for cloud provider controls (IaaS/PaaS) or inclusive, and what responsibilities Aurora retains (network, key mgmt, backups).

Can you confirm you can provide these items and point us to an evidence link? We prefer a single bundle (PDF + CSV) and a brief note on scope so our auditors can map responsibilities.

Thanks,
Elena
Procurement Lead, Aurora Health

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Elena Soto <elena.soto@aurorahealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: SOC 2 Type II + bridge letter + subprocessor list (Aurora onboarding)

Hi Elena,

Thanks for the clear checklist — we can absolutely support that timeline. High-level answers and next steps below; I'll loop in compliance for the specific language.

1) SOC 2 Type II: attached is the redacted SOC 2 Type II report for the period ending 2025-12-31 (file: Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2025.pdf).  If you need the full unredacted copy for auditors we can arrange an NDA conduit.

2) Bridge letter: we have a standard bridge-letter template we can populate to cover the gap if your audit window extends beyond the report period; see attached BridgeLetter-template.docx. If you can confirm the exact audit window (dates your auditors need covered) we will draft the completed letter within 48 business hours.

3) Subprocessor list: attached CSV (subprocessor_list_2026-07.csv) contains our current list. Important note: some cloud controls are shared — we rely on our cloud provider's SOCs for physical and infrastructure controls.

4) Carve-out / scope: Redwood's SOC is a carve-out model with respect to cloud provider managed controls (we document the mapping in the attached CSV and in the SOC report's subservice organization section). Practically: GCP's (or customer's chosen cloud) SOC covers infrastructure/physical, while Redwood is responsible for application layer, encryption-in-transit, and operational procedures. We'll add a short paragraph in the bridge letter explicitly mapping responsibilities for Aurora's auditors.

Next steps: 
- Can you confirm the audit window Aurora needs covered (start/end dates)?
- Do your auditors need an unredacted SOC or is the redacted PDF sufficient?
- Any specific wording required by your procurement/audit team for the bridge letter?

Cc'ing Karthik (infra/compliance) and Mina (customer compliance) to assist with the technical mapping and final sign-off.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Head of Customer Security Programs, Redwood Inference
sofia.ivanova@redwood.com
Attachments: Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2025.pdf (redacted), BridgeLetter-template.docx, subprocessor_list_2026-07.csv

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Elena Soto <elena.soto@aurorahealth.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 08:31:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: SOC 2 Type II + bridge letter + subprocessor list (Aurora onboarding)

Elena / Sofia — quick technical clarifications to include in the bridge letter and the mapping CSV: 

- Cloud carve-out specifics: Redwood's SOC references GCP (primary production) as a subservice organization for infrastructure and physical security (carve-out). That means GCP SOC covers: data center physical security, hypervisor-level isolation, certain networking fabric controls, and host OS patching where performed by the cloud provider. 
- Redwood controls (in-scope): VM/container runtime configuration, application auth, key rotation processes (note: customer-managed KMS integrations are supported — if Aurora uses its own KMS we will document who holds keys), data encryption-at-rest for Redwood-managed volumes, application logs, incident response, and backups (Redwood performs application-level backups, but we also rely on cloud storage snapshot primitives).
- Subprocessor coverage: the attached CSV flags which subprocessors are "covered-by-subservice-SOC" vs "not-covered". Example: GCP's SOC covers compute/storage infra; our monitoring provider (EdgeWatch) is NOT covered by the cloud provider SOC and is listed as a separate subprocessor with controls evidence.
- Recommended bridge-letter phrasing (draft outline): short affirmation of no material changes in control environment since the SOC period end, explicit mention of carve-out for cloud provider controls, and a pointer to the CSV for subprocessor mapping. 

I can draft the language for the bridge letter. Sofia — if you approve, I'll prepare a one-paragraph draft and attach it to the template for Mina / legal to review.

-Karthik
Sr. Director, Infrastructure Security, Redwood Inference

From: Elena Soto <elena.soto@aurorahealth.com>

Thanks,
Elena
